what: Symbol-to-capability traceability (DESIGN.md section 4). Written by build_traceability.py; do not edit by hand. Plans, not results.

existing.X1: a phone of the speaking module
existing.X2: formants and bandwidths moved against the module phone (f1-f4, g1-g4, b1-b4, reach)
existing.X4: stop timing and release (vot, asp, lead, bar, voi, burst, noburst, pre, ej, impl)
existing.X5: a sound the accent layer makes beside a vowel (<, >, ms, hush, whisper)
existing.X6: tap: brief closures cut into a sound (tap, tapms)
existing.X7: phonation keys (oq, tl, creak, whisper, brth)
existing.X10: stress: the module's stress digits and the accent line
existing.X11: tone lines and the layer's own pitch (tone, f0=own)
existing.X13: syllables and pieces in the annotation; an affricate said as stop + fricative (says)

to_build.C1: never silent: a diagnostics channel and a strict mode
to_build.C2: the IPA reader and segment model
to_build.C3: the master table, its validator and the adapter (composition when a pack is built)
to_build.C4: composition when speaking, with nearest-feature fallback and a loud warning
to_build.C5: pitch: register steps, a slope per phrase, pitch moved by a consonant under own pitch
to_build.C6: phonation held through a sound or at its edges; breath noise on voiced frames
to_build.C7: syllabicity: a consonant as a syllable, a vowel as none
to_build.C8: edge transforms on the neighbouring phone (spreading)
to_build.C9: the nasal and the second pole/zero pair, set directly
to_build.C10: timed events on a carrier phone
to_build.C11: aperture modulation at a stated rate (trills)
to_build.C12: transient excitation: an impulse into the resonators

tests.T-stop: closure length, burst spectrum, voice onset time, F2/F3 at the vowel edge, in a_a i_i u_u
tests.T-fric: noise centre and band edges (0 to 5.5 kHz), length, voicing
tests.T-approx: F1-F3 mid-sound and their movement into the vowel
tests.T-trill: modulation rate in Hz, depth in dB, number of closures
tests.T-vowel: F1-F3 at the midpoint against the reference range; length
tests.T-click: silent closure, burst length and level against the vowel, spectrum by place, no breath
tests.T-airstream: implosive: voicing that grows through the closure, weak burst; ejective: silence after the burst, no breath
tests.T-phonation: H1-H2, harmonics-to-noise, period regularity, against the plain sound
tests.T-nasality: A1-P0, F1 bandwidth, against the plain vowel
tests.T-shift: the named formant or noise measure moves the stated way against the plain base
tests.T-length: length ratio against the plain base
tests.T-syllable: number of syllable peaks; length of the marked sound
tests.T-release: burst absent, or replaced by a murmur or a lateral, at the release
tests.T-stress: pitch, length and level of the marked syllable against an unmarked one
tests.T-tone: F0 contour against the points asked, in semitones; order of the levels
tests.T-register: the tones after the mark sit lower (or higher) by the step asked
tests.T-slope: slope of F0 across the phrase, against the unmarked phrase
tests.T-boundary: pause, final lengthening and boundary pitch; or their absence
tests.T-sequence: the two parts in order, one closure, length less than the two apart
tests.T-contrast: measurably different from its nearest neighbour, in the right direction

rows.name: voiceless: the sound is produced without vocal-fold vibration (devoicing of a normally voiced segment)
rows.how: base + voiceless: voicing off; a sonorant or vowel becomes breath through the same shape

rows.name: voiceless (alternative placement above a symbol with a descender)
rows.how: base + voiceless: voicing off; a sonorant or vowel becomes breath through the same shape

rows.name: voiced: vocal-fold vibration during a segment that is normally voiceless
rows.how: base + voiced: voicing through the closure or the friction

rows.name: aspirated: a period of voicelessness (open glottis) after the release before voicing of the following sound begins
rows.how: base + aspirated: a longer voice onset time filled with breath

rows.name: more rounded: greater lip rounding than the base symbol implies
rows.how: base + more rounded: F2 and F3 lowered one step

rows.name: less rounded: less lip rounding than the base symbol implies
rows.how: base + less rounded: F2 and F3 raised one step

rows.name: advanced: articulated further forward than the base symbol implies
rows.how: base + advanced: a vowel's F2 raised; a consonant moved part of the way to the next place forward

rows.name: retracted: articulated further back than the base symbol implies
rows.how: base + retracted: the reverse

rows.name: centralized: tongue position moved toward the centre of the vowel space on the front–back dimension
rows.how: base + centralized: F2 moved part of the way to the central vowel of the same height

rows.name: mid-centralized: moved toward the mid-central (schwa) position, in height as well as backness
rows.how: base + mid-centralized: F1 and F2 moved part of the way to schwa

rows.name: syllabic: the consonant forms the nucleus of a syllable
rows.how: base + syllabic: the consonant carries the syllable, its stress and its tone, with no vowel put in

rows.name: non-syllabic: the vowel is not the syllable nucleus (e.g. the off-glide of a diphthong)
rows.how: base + non-syllabic: the vowel is short, carries no syllable and glides into its neighbour

rows.name: rhoticity: r-colouring of a vowel (tongue tip raised/retroflexed or tongue bunched, often with pharyngeal constriction)
rows.how: base + rhotic: F3 lowered towards F2

rows.name: breathy voiced: vocal folds vibrate with lower tension and incomplete closure, letting more air escape (murmur)
rows.how: base + breathy: a longer open phase, more tilt and breath noise through the whole sound

rows.name: creaky voiced: constricted glottis with slow, irregular vocal-fold vibration (laryngealization)
rows.how: base + creaky: a shorter open phase and alternating periods

rows.name: linguolabial: tongue tip or blade against the upper lip
rows.how: base + linguolabial: locus and noise between the bilabial and the alveolar

rows.name: labialized: secondary lip rounding (often with raised tongue back) added to the consonant
rows.how: base + labialized: F2 and F3 lowered at the release, a brief w-like glide

rows.name: palatalized: secondary raising of the tongue body toward the hard palate
rows.how: base + palatalized: F2 raised at the release, a brief j-like glide

rows.name: velarized: secondary raising of the back of the tongue toward the velum
rows.how: base + velarized: F2 lowered

rows.name: pharyngealized: secondary constriction of the pharynx (tongue root/epiglottis retracted)
rows.how: base + pharyngealized: F1 raised and F2 lowered, reaching into the vowels beside it

rows.name: velarized or pharyngealized: a cover mark for velarization, uvularization or pharyngealization, written through the letter
rows.how: base + velarized or pharyngealized (velarized unless a pack says otherwise)

rows.name: raised: articulated with a closer constriction (higher tongue) than the base symbol implies
rows.how: base + raised: a vowel's F1 lowered; an approximant gains friction

rows.name: lowered: articulated with a more open constriction (lower tongue) than the base symbol implies
rows.how: base + lowered: a vowel's F1 raised; a fricative loses its friction

rows.name: advanced tongue root (ATR): tongue root moved forward and larynx lowered, expanding the pharynx
rows.how: base + advanced tongue root: F1 lowered

rows.name: retracted tongue root (RTR): tongue root pulled back, narrowing the pharynx
rows.how: base + retracted tongue root: F1 raised

rows.name: dental: tongue tip or blade against the upper teeth
rows.how: base + dental: locus and noise of the dental place

rows.name: apical: articulated with the tongue tip
rows.how: base + apical: a small shift of the noise or burst spectrum (marked approximate)

rows.name: laminal: articulated with the tongue blade
rows.how: base + laminal: a small shift of the noise or burst spectrum (marked approximate)

rows.name: nasalized: the velum is lowered so air resonates in the nasal cavity as well as the mouth
rows.how: base + nasalized: the nose opened

rows.name: nasal release: the oral closure of a stop is released by lowering the velum, so air escapes through the nose (e.g. English sudden)
rows.how: base + nasal release: the stop is not released by a burst but into a brief nasal of its own place

rows.name: lateral release: the stop is released by lowering the sides of the tongue into a lateral (e.g. English middle)
rows.how: base + lateral release: the stop is released into l

rows.name: no audible release: the stop closure is held without an audible release burst (unreleased / checked stop)
rows.how: base + no audible release: the burst left out

rows.name: Marks the syllable that carries the word's main stress. The mark is written before the stressed syllable, not before its vowel.
rows.how: main stress of the syllable that follows

rows.name: Marks a syllable that is stressed relative to unstressed syllables but less strongly than the primary-stressed one. Written before the syllable.
rows.how: secondary stress of the syllable that follows

rows.name: The preceding segment (vowel or consonant) is held longer. On a consonant it marks a long consonant (geminate).
rows.how: base + long: a vowel's length, a consonant's hold

rows.name: The preceding segment is somewhat longer than short but shorter than long.
rows.how: base + half-long

rows.name: The segment under the mark (usually a vowel) is extra short while keeping its quality. On a consonant the breve can stand for a very brief articulation, for example a flap that has no letter of its own.
rows.how: base + extra-short

rows.name: Boundary of a minor prosodic group (foot group). It is a phrasing mark, not an articulation.
rows.how: the end of a minor group: a continuation ending with little or no pause

rows.name: Boundary of a major prosodic group (intonation phrase). Often coincides with a breath or pause.
rows.how: the end of a major group: a final ending and a pause

rows.name: Marks where one syllable ends and the next begins. On the chart it separates two vowels in hiatus (re.act), which are therefore not a diphthong.
rows.how: a syllable break

rows.name: Two words are joined with no break between them, for example a linking or liaison consonant that becomes the onset of the next word's syllable (French les amis /lɛ.z‿a.mi/), or two words forming one phonological unit (hot dog /ˈhɒt‿dɒɡ/).
rows.how: two words said as one piece, with no break

rows.name: downstep: the following tone (typically a high tone) is realised on a lower pitch register than the same tone before it, and that lowered register persists for following tones; written before the affected syllable
rows.how: a step down of the register: every later tone of the phrase is lower

rows.name: upstep: the following tone is realised on a higher pitch register than the same tone before it; also used for pitch reset at the start of a new prosodic chunk; written before the affected syllable
rows.how: a step up of the register

rows.name: global rise: intonation, not lexical tone; the whole prosodic unit (when attached to a boundary mark such as ‖) or the marked word/syllable has rising overall pitch
rows.how: the pitch of the whole group rises

rows.name: global fall: intonation, not lexical tone; the whole prosodic unit (when attached to a boundary mark) or the marked word/syllable has falling overall pitch
rows.how: the pitch of the whole group falls
